children: The FTSE MIB rose over 1% to around 52,000 on Friday, rebounding from a four-week low, as easing oil prices offered some respite to markets.
Crude prices paused their recent rally after the US and Iran were reportedly exploring a phased agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
At home, Italy's government will meet domestic refiners next month to discuss boosting fuel production in a bid to ease prices, with Eni and Saras among those invited.

Across the board, gains were broad-based, spearheaded by heavyweight financials amid merger talks, including UniCredit (+1.8%), Intesa Sanpaolo (+1.2%), Assicurazioni Generali (+1.4%), Banco BPM (+2.1%), BPER Banca (+1.8%) and MPS (+1.4%).
Other notable gainers included technology shares STMicroelectronics and Prysmian, both advancing more than 2%.
For the week, the benchmark index is heading for a modest gain.

title: FTSE MIB Rebounds on Friday
